newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Handlowy to buy Opalenica sugar refinery. [CORRECTED 12:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland's Handlowy to buy Opalenica sugar refinery. [CORRECTED 12:48 GMT]

text.p: Poland's commercial Bank Handlowy SA will buy a 70 percent stake in the Opalenica sugar refinery in western Poland for about 40 million zlotys over the next five years, the refinery's president said on Friday.

Stanislaw Gnacy (Corrects spelling from Gancy) told Reuters Opalenica would also convert its eight million zloty debts into shares for its creditors -- the cooperative Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA, Bank Rozwoju Cukrownictwa SA and the trading company Rolimpex SA.
"Shareholders decided to raise Opalenica's capital by a debt-for-equity swap and to issue new shares to be taken over by Bank Handlowy over the next five years," Gnacy said.
Opalenica's current shareholders are the Poznansko-Pomorska Spolka Cukrowa SA sugar holding with a 51 percent stake and the state treasury with a 49 percent stake.

Gnacy said that after the capital rise is completed Handlowy would hold 70 percent of shares, BGZ, Bank Rozwoju Cukrownictwa and Rolimpex would have about 20 percent and the sugar holding and treasury the rest.
After the Handlowy investment is completed in five years, the capital of Opalenica, which employes 300, will be 54 million zlotys against the current 5.6 million zlotys.

Gnacy said Opalenica had a net profit of about 3.8 million zlotys and a gross profit of about six million zlotys in the accounting year ending on September 30, 1996 on production of 23,700 tonnes of sugar.
